You will need: Multiple choice answer sheet Soft clean eraser Soft pencil (type B or HB is recommended) INSTRUCTIONS  There are thirty questions on this paper. Answer all questions.  For each question there are four possible answers A, B, C and D. Choose the one you consider correct and record your choice in soft pencil on the multiple choice answer sheet.  Follow the instructions on the multiple choice answer sheet.  Write in soft pencil.  Write your name, centre number and candidate number on the multiple choice answer sheet in the spaces provided unless this has been done for you.  Do not use correction fluid.  Do not write on any bar codes.  You may use a calculator. INFORMATION  The total mark for this paper is 30.  Each correct answer will score one mark.  Any rough working should be done on this question paper.
Jamie wants full ownership of the business.
Jamie wants to avoid the risk of losing personal assets. Which type of business should Jamie choose?

The following information relates to the non-current assets of a business that was formed three years ago. $ cost at start of year 1 10 000 accumulated depreciation at end of year 3 6 000 draft profit for year 3 18 000 In calculating the draft profit for year 3, depreciation has been consistently charged using the straight-line method. Prior to finalising the accounts, the business decided to change the method of depreciation for year 3 to the reducing balance method at a rate of 25% per annum. What was the revised profit for year 3?
Why does a business maintain a sales ledger control account?

options.A: to ensure that statements are sent out promptly to customers
options.B: to record the total of discounts received
options.C: to reduce the risk of irrecoverable debts
options.D: to verify the arithmetical accuracy of entries in the sales ledger

questions.questionText: Iga is worried that her book-keeper may have been forgetting to record credit notes received. What should she do to find out?
A trial balance does not balance and a suspense account is opened. On investigation, the following errors are found.

The table shows extracts from a business’s bank reconciliation. $ balance per cash book at 31 December 2075 debit balance per bank statement at 31 December 2250 credit bank charges per bank statement not entered in cash book 150 outstanding cheques not presented at year end 325 What is the bank balance to be shown in the financial statements?

The total of trade payables balances in Konrad’s purchases ledger was $57 400. The following errors were then discovered. $ discount allowed overcast in cash book 2000 returns outwards omitted in a supplier’s account 350 payments to trade payables undercast in cash book 137 purchases journal overcast 500 What is the correct total of trade payables balances?
Which statement is not correct?

options.A: Control accounts reveal whether there are errors in sales and purchases ledgers.
options.B: Credit balances in a sales ledger are trade receivables.
options.C: Debit balances in a purchases ledger are current assets.
options.D: A sales ledger control account includes irrecoverable debts.

questions.questionText: A business maintains an allowance for irrecoverable debts of 5% of trade receivables. At the end of the current financial year, trade receivables totalled $8000 which was 20% less than the year before. How will the profit for the current financial year be affected by the change in the allowance for irrecoverable debts?
A trader does not keep full records but supplies the following information.
Which statement(s) are true of drawings?

Vikram is a partner in a business. Partners do not receive salaries or interest on capital, but they are charged 5% interest on the balance of their drawings account. Vikram made drawings of $40 000 during the year and his share of profits was $47 500. His current account showed a credit balance of $4500 after the relevant entries were made at the end of the financial year. What was the debit balance on Vikram’s current account at the beginning of the financial year?
A partnership operates without having a partnership agreement. Which rules will apply to the partnership?

L and M are in partnership, sharing profits and losses in the ratio of 3 : 2 respectively. The following information was available at year end. L M $ $ capital 200 000 150 000 interest on capital 8% drawings 30 000 20 000 interest on drawings 5% partners’ salaries 22 000 17 000 The residual profit shared by L was $24 000. What was the profit for the year before appropriation?
Which statements about debenture interest are correct?

A company has the following reserves. $ share premium 60 000 revaluation reserve 75 000 general reserve 10 000 retained earnings 21 500 The directors wish to make a bonus issue of ordinary shares of $1 each. What is the maximum number of bonus shares which the company could possibly issue?

A business provided the information shown for a period. $ sales revenue 1 500 000 purchases 1 000 000 inventory at end of the period 50 000 The rate of inventory turnover for the period was 12 times and the business attained a gross profit margin of 40%. The business also made some purchases returns and incurred an amount for carriage inwards. What was the value of inventory at the beginning of the period?
When comparing with the previous year, a trader finds that his gross profit margin has increased and his trade receivables turnover has decreased. Which statement would explain this?

options.A: He bought in bulk and passed the savings on to his customers who bought more.
options.B: He offered more trade discount and more customers paid in cash.
options.C: He raised his selling price and offered more cash discounts.
options.D: He reduced his selling price to increase the total value of sales.

questions.questionText: B Limited had credit sales for the year of $3 285 000 and trade receivables at year end of $405 000. The sales director believed that if cash discounts had been given, then trade receivables would have been $351 000. The allowance for irrecoverable debts would have been reduced by $9000. What difference would the discounts have made to the trade receivables turnover?

options.A: It would have been 5 days faster.
options.B: It would have been 5 days slower.
options.C: It would have been 6 days faster.
options.D: It would have been 6 days slower.

questions.questionText: Abusinessmakesweddingdresses.Eachmachinistispaid$30adayandeachsupervisor$40a day. Each supervisor can work with up to 10 machinists and each machinist can produce one wedding dress a day. If 95 wedding dresses a day are produced, what is the daily labour cost?
Which statement best describes variable costs?

options.A: costs that are the same in total up to a certain level then increase with output
options.B: costs that are the same in total over any output level
options.C: costs that are constant per unit as output increases
options.D: costs that increase per unit as output increases

questions.questionText: P Limited makes wooden chairs at a unit cost of $70 each. It has received an order to produce a batch of 1000 wooden chairs with padded seats. This requires $6000 of additional materials, an extra 500 labour hours at $15 per hour and a $2000 increase in overheads. What is the cost of the batch?
Why would overheads be over absorbed?

options.A: Overheads absorbed is less than overheads budgeted.
options.B: Overheads absorbed is more than overheads budgeted.
options.C: Overheads incurred is less than overheads absorbed.
options.D: Overheads incurred is more than overheads absorbed.

questions.questionText: A company makes one product with a selling price of $384 per unit. The costs are as follows: per unit direct materials 4 kilos at $8 per kilo direct labour 8 hours at $12 per hour selling and distribution $40 The mark-up is 50%. What is the factory overhead absorption rate per labour hour?
Which statements about marginal costing are correct?

A company makes and sells a single type of product. The budgeted information for 6000 units is as follows: $ variable manufacturing costs 90 000 variable selling expenses 6 000 fixed manufacturing overheads 54 000 fixed administrative overheads 21 000 The unit selling price is $40. How many units must the company produce and sell to achieve a target profit of $45 000?
The diagram shows a break-even chart. X sales revenue revenue total cost and costs $ Y fixed cost level of activity budgeted level of activity What does line XY represent?

options.B: the margin of safety in terms of revenue
options.D: the total contribution at break-even point

questions.questionText: What is not an assumption in cost–volume–profit analysis?

options.A: The unit fixed cost is constant.
options.B: The unit selling price is constant.
options.C: The unit variable cost is constant.
